seclai

Seclai Python SDK.

Provides synchronous and asynchronous clients for the Seclai API.

Quick start::

from seclai import Seclai

client = Seclai(api_key="...")
agents = client.list_agents()

All public symbols are re-exported from this package:

  • Seclai — synchronous client
  • AsyncSeclai — asynchronous client
  • SeclaiError — base exception
  • SeclaiConfigurationError — configuration errors
  • SeclaiAPIStatusError — non-2xx HTTP responses
  • SeclaiAPIValidationError — HTTP 422 validation errors
  • SeclaiStreamingError — SSE stream errors
  • AgentRunStreamRequest — typed request body for streaming runs
  • JSONValue — recursive JSON type alias
  • ApiVersion — dated API versions this release was built against
  • DEFAULT_API_VERSION / LATEST_API_VERSION — the baseline and newest known version
  • unwrap_items() — read a version-gated list response in either shape

class AsyncSeclai(seclai.seclai._SeclaiBase): 
5230class AsyncSeclai(_SeclaiBase):
5231    """Seclai asynchronous client.
5232
5233    Most users should prefer the typed convenience methods (e.g. `run_agent`, `list_sources`)
5234    which raise SDK exceptions on failures.
5235
5236    This client can be used as an async context manager:
5237
5238        async with AsyncSeclai(api_key="...") as client:
5239            sources = await client.list_sources()
5240    """
5241
5242    def __init__(
5243        self,
5244        *,
5245        api_key: str | None = None,
5246        access_token: str | Callable[[], str | Awaitable[str]] | None = None,
5247        timeout: float = 30.0,
5248        api_key_header: str = "x-api-key",
5249        default_headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
5250        http_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
5251        profile: str | None = None,
5252        config_dir: str | None = None,
5253        auto_refresh: bool = True,
5254        account_id: str | None = None,
5255        api_version: str | None = None,
5256        allow_unknown_api_version: bool = False,
5257    ) -> None:
5258        """Create an asynchronous Seclai client.
5259
5260        Credentials are resolved via a chain (first match wins):
5261
5262        1. Explicit ``api_key``
5263        2. Explicit ``access_token`` (static string or provider callable)
5264        3. ``SECLAI_API_KEY`` environment variable
5265        4. SSO profile from ``~/.seclai/config`` + cached tokens
5266
5267        Args:
5268            api_key: API key used for authentication. If omitted, ``SECLAI_API_KEY`` is used.
5269            access_token: Static bearer token string or a callable returning one
5270                (sync or async). Mutually exclusive with ``api_key``.
5271            timeout: Request timeout (seconds).
5272            api_key_header: Header name to use for the API key.
5273            default_headers: Extra headers to include on every request.
5274            http_client: Optional pre-configured ``httpx.AsyncClient`` to use. A
5275                ``Seclai-Version`` among its default headers is checked as one
5276                in ``default_headers`` is, at construction and on each request.
5277                The typed methods that go through the generated client do not
5278                use this client.
5279            profile: SSO profile name from ``~/.seclai/config``.
5280            config_dir: Override the config directory path.
5281            auto_refresh: Auto-refresh expired SSO tokens. Defaults to ``True``.
5282            account_id: Target organization account ID (``X-Account-Id`` header).
5283            api_version: Dated API version (``YYYY-MM-DD``) sent as the
5284                ``Seclai-Version`` header, opting into backward-incompatible
5285                changes released on or before that date. Omitted by default,
5286                so upgrading the SDK alone never changes response shapes.
5287
5288        Raises:
5289            SeclaiConfigurationError: If no credentials are found.
5290        """
5291        super().__init__(
5292            api_key=api_key,
5293            access_token=access_token,
5294            timeout=timeout,
5295            api_key_header=api_key_header,
5296            default_headers=default_headers,
5297            profile=profile,
5298            config_dir=config_dir,
5299            auto_refresh=auto_refresh,
5300            account_id=account_id,
5301            api_version=api_version,
5302            allow_unknown_api_version=allow_unknown_api_version,
5303        )
5304        self._client = http_client or httpx.AsyncClient(
5305            base_url=SECLAI_API_URL,
5306            timeout=self._options.timeout,
5307            headers=self._default_headers(),
5308        )
5309        self._owns_client = http_client is None
5310        if http_client is not None:
5311            _validate_client_version(
5312                self._options, self._default_headers(), http_client.headers
5313            )
5314
5315    async def aclose(self) -> None:
5316        """Close underlying HTTP resources owned by this client.
5317
5318        If you created the client with a custom ``http_client``, this is a no-op
5319        for that client (you remain responsible for closing it).
5320        """
5321        if self._owns_client:
5322            await self._client.aclose()
5323        if self._owns_generated_client and self._generated_client_instance is not None:
5324            await self._generated_client_instance.get_async_httpx_client().aclose()
5325
5326    async def __aenter__(self) -> Self:
5327        """Enter an async context manager and return self."""
5328        return self
5329
5330    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type: object, exc: object, tb: object) -> None:
5331        """Exit the async context manager and close resources.
5332
5333        Args:
5334            exc_type: Exception type (if any).
5335            exc: Exception instance (if any).
5336            tb: Traceback (if any).
5337        """
5338        await self.aclose()
5339
5340    async def request(
5341        self,
5342        method: str,
5343        path: str,
5344        *,
5345        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
5346        json: JSONValue | None = None,
5347        headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
5348    ) -> JSONValue | str | None:
5349        """Make a raw HTTP request to the Seclai API.
5350
5351        This is a low-level escape hatch. For most operations, prefer the typed
5352        convenience methods on this client.
5353
5354        Args:
5355            method: HTTP method (e.g. `"GET"`, `"POST"`).
5356            path: Request path relative to `SECLAI_API_URL` (e.g. `"/sources/"`).
5357            params: Query parameters.
5358            json: JSON body to send.
5359            headers: Per-request header overrides.
5360
5361        Returns:
5362            Parsed JSON for JSON responses, raw text for non-JSON responses, or `None` for empty bodies.
5363
5364        Raises:
5365            SeclaiAPIStatusError: If the response status code is not successful.
5366        """
5367        response = await self._client.request(
5368            method,
5369            path,
5370            params=params,
5371            json=json,
5372            headers=await _merge_request_headers_async(
5373                options=self._options,
5374                client_headers=self._client.headers,
5375                request_headers=headers,
5376            ),
5377        )
5378        _raise_for_status(response)
5379        if not response.content:
5380            return None
5381        content_type = response.headers.get("content-type", "")
5382        if "application/json" in content_type:
5383            return cast(JSONValue, response.json())
5384        return response.text
5385
5386    async def run_agent(self, agent_id: str, body: AgentRunRequest) -> AgentRunResponse:
5387        """Run an agent.
5388
5389        Starts a new agent run for the given agent and returns the run record.
5390
5391        Args:
5392            agent_id: Agent identifier.
5393            body: Agent run request payload.
5394
5395        Returns:
5396            The created agent run.
5397
5398        Raises:
5399            SeclaiAPIValidationError: If the API returns a validation error.
5400            SeclaiAPIStatusError: If the API returns a non-success status code.
5401        """
5402        from seclai._generated.api.agents.run_agent_api_agents_agent_id_runs_post import (
5403            asyncio_detailed,
5404        )
5405
5406        path = f"/agents/{agent_id}/runs"
5407        response = await asyncio_detailed(
5408            agent_id=agent_id, client=(await self._async_generated_client()), body=body
5409        )
5410        self._raise_for_openapi_response(
5411            method="POST",
5412            path=path,
5413            response=response,
5414            ok_statuses={HTTPStatus.OK},
5415        )
5416        if response.parsed is None:
5417            raise SeclaiAPIStatusError(
5418                message="Empty response",
5419                status_code=int(response.status_code),
5420                method="POST",
5421                url=self._build_url(path),
5422                response_text=None,
5423            )
5424        parsed = response.parsed
5425        if isinstance(parsed, HTTPValidationError):
5426            raise SeclaiAPIValidationError(
5427                message="Validation error",
5428                status_code=int(response.status_code),
5429                method="POST",
5430                url=self._build_url(path),
5431                response_text=None,

5439    async def run_streaming_agent_and_wait(
5440        self,
5441        agent_id: str,
5442        body: AgentRunStreamRequest,
5443        *,
5444        timeout: float | None = None,
5445        headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
5446    ) -> AgentRunResponse:
5447        """Run an agent via SSE streaming and block until completion (async).
5448
5449        This uses POST /agents/{agent_id}/runs/stream and consumes Server-Sent Events (SSE).
5450        The method returns when an `event: done` message is received.
5451        """
5452        import json as _json
5453        import time as _time
5454
5455        path = f"/agents/{agent_id}/runs/stream"
5456
5457        merged_headers = await _merge_request_headers_async(
5458            options=self._options,
5459            client_headers=self._client.headers,
5460            request_headers=headers,
5461        )
5462        _setdefault_header(merged_headers, "accept", "text/event-stream")
5463
5464        timeout_seconds = self._options.timeout if timeout is None else timeout
5465        start = _time.monotonic()
5466
5467        try:
5468            async with self._client.stream(
5469                "POST",
5470                path,
5471                json=body,
5472                headers=merged_headers,
5473                timeout=timeout_seconds,
5474            ) as response:
5475                if response.status_code >= 400:
5476                    # Lazy body inside `stream()`; read it so the error carries
5477                    # its text and a 422 its field-level detail.
5478                    await response.aread()
5479                _raise_for_status(response)
5480
5481                current_event: str | None = None
5482                data_lines: list[str] = []
5483                last_seen: AgentRunResponse | None = None
5484
5485                def dispatch() -> AgentRunResponse | None:
5486                    nonlocal current_event, data_lines, last_seen
5487                    if current_event is None and not data_lines:
5488                        return None
5489                    data = "\n".join(data_lines)
5490                    evt = current_event
5491                    current_event = None
5492                    data_lines = []
5493                    if not data:
5494                        return None
5495                    if evt not in {"init", "done"}:
5496                        return None
5497                    try:
5498                        parsed_dict = cast(dict[str, Any], _json.loads(data))
5499                        parsed = AgentRunResponse.from_dict(parsed_dict)
5500                        last_seen = parsed
5501                        if evt == "done":
5502                            return parsed
5503                    except Exception:
5504                        return None
5505                    return None
5506
5507                async for line in response.aiter_lines():
5508                    if _time.monotonic() - start > timeout_seconds:
5509                        raise SeclaiError(
5510                            f"Timed out after {timeout_seconds}s waiting for streaming agent run to complete."
5511                        )
5512
5513                    if line == "":
5514                        done = dispatch()
5515                        if done is not None:
5516                            return done
5517                        continue
5518                    if line.startswith(":"):
5519                        continue
5520                    if line.startswith("event:"):
5521                        current_event = line[len("event:") :].strip() or None
5522                        continue
5523                    if line.startswith("data:"):
5524                        data_lines.append(line[len("data:") :].lstrip())
5525                        continue
5526
5527                done = dispatch()
5528                if done is not None:
5529                    return done
5530                if last_seen is not None:
5531                    return last_seen
5532                raise SeclaiError("Stream ended before receiving a 'done' event.")
5533        except httpx.TimeoutException as e:
5534            raise SeclaiError(
5535                f"Timed out after {timeout_seconds}s waiting for streaming agent run to complete."

6131    async def upload_file_to_content(

6171        created_payload: BinaryIO | None = None

6173            upload_file: File

6176            elif isinstance(file, (str, os.PathLike)):
6177                file_path = Path(file)

6179                resolved_mime_type = mime_type or _guess_mime_type(resolved_file_name)
6180                created_payload = file_path.open("rb")
6181                upload_file = File(
6182                    payload=created_payload,
6183                    file_name=resolved_file_name,
6184                    mime_type=resolved_mime_type,
6185                )
6186            elif isinstance(file, bytes):
6187                created_payload = BytesIO(file)
6188                resolved_mime_type = mime_type or _guess_mime_type(file_name)
6189                upload_file = File(
6190                    payload=created_payload,
6191                    file_name=file_name,
6192                    mime_type=resolved_mime_type,
6193                )
6194            else:
6195                resolved_mime_type = mime_type or _guess_mime_type(file_name)
6196                upload_file = File(

6198                    file_name=file_name,

6223                    method="POST",

6255    async def get_api_version(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
6256        """Get the API version this request resolved to, and the versions available.
6257
6258        Returns:
6259            ``pinned_version`` (the account's sticky pin, or ``None``),
6260            ``effective_version`` for THIS request, plus ``default_version``,
6261            ``latest_version`` and ``known_versions``. Resolution order is the
6262            ``Seclai-Version`` header, then the account pin, then the default, so
6263            ``effective_version`` reflects the client's ``api_version`` when set.
6264        """
6265        return cast(dict[str, Any], await self.request("GET", "/version"))
6266
6267    async def update_api_version(self, version: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
6268        """Pin the account to a dated API version, or clear the pin.
6269
6270        Owner/admin only.
6271
6272        Args:
6273            version: A ``YYYY-MM-DD`` date to pin to, or ``None`` to clear the pin
6274                and revert to the default baseline.
6275
6276        Returns:
6277            The updated version state. ``effective_version`` describes this
6278            request, not the pin just written — a ``Seclai-Version`` header still
6279            overrides the pin.
6280
6281        Raises:
6282            SeclaiConfigurationError: If ``version`` is one this release was not
6283                built against. The pin is account-wide and sticky, so an unknown
6284                version here would silently reshape responses for every
6285                header-less caller on the account, not just this client — a wider
6286                blast radius than the ``api_version`` option the constructor
6287                already guards. Pass ``allow_unknown_api_version=True`` to the
6288                client to override.
6289        """
6290        try:
6291            validate_api_version(
6292                version, allow_unknown=self._options.allow_unknown_api_version
6293            )
6294        except ValueError as e:
6295            raise SeclaiConfigurationError(str(e)) from e
6296        return cast(
6297            dict[str, Any],
6298            await self.request("PUT", "/version", json={"version": version}),
6299        )

6622    async def download_agent_run_attachment(
6623        self,
6624        run_id: str,
6625        attachment_id: str,
6626        *,
6627        download_name: str | None = None,
6628    ) -> httpx.Response:
6629        """Download an attachment emitted by a step in an agent run.
6630
6631        Returns a **streaming** response. The caller is responsible for
6632        consuming and closing the response::
6633
6634            response = await client.download_agent_run_attachment("run", "att")
6635            async with response:
6636                async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
6637                    f.write(chunk)
6638
6639        Args:
6640            run_id: Run identifier.
6641            attachment_id: URL-safe-base64-encoded ``storage_key`` of the
6642                attachment (as surfaced in webhook/email payloads and run
6643                output manifests).
6644            download_name: Optional filename hint for the download disposition.
6645
6646        Returns:
6647            A streaming ``httpx.Response``. Must be closed by the caller.
6648        """
6649        headers = await _merge_request_headers_async(
6650            options=self._options,
6651            client_headers=self._client.headers,
6652            request_headers=None,
6653        )
6654        request = self._client.build_request(
6655            "GET",
6656            f"/v2/agent-runs/{run_id}/attachments/{attachment_id}",
6657            params=_strip_none({"download_name": download_name}),
6658            headers=headers,
6659        )
6660        response = await self._client.send(request, stream=True)
6661        if response.is_error:
6662            # Read the body for a useful error message, then release the
6663            # connection before raising — the caller never receives the
6664            # streaming response on the error path.
6665            await response.aread()
6666            await response.aclose()
6667            _raise_for_status(response)
6668        return response

6781    async def list_evaluation_criteria(
6782        self, agent_id: str, *, page: int = 1, limit: int = 50
6783    ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
6784        """List evaluation criteria for an agent.
6785
6786        Args:
6787            agent_id: Agent identifier.
6788            page: Page number (1-indexed). **Ignored** unless the client opts in
6789                with ``api_version="2026-07-27"`` or later — the legacy response
6790                is unpaginated and always contains every criterion, so a
6791                paginate-until-empty loop over it never terminates.
6792            limit: Items per page. Ignored on the legacy shape, as above.
6793
6794        Returns:
6795            The evaluation criteria. Either wire shape is accepted: a bare array
6796            by default, the canonical ``{data, pagination}`` envelope once opted
6797            in. Use :meth:`list_evaluation_criteria_page` for the metadata.
6798        """
6799        page_result = await self.list_evaluation_criteria_page(
6800            agent_id, page=page, limit=limit
6801        )
6802        return unwrap_items(page_result)
6803
6804    async def list_evaluation_criteria_page(
6805        self, agent_id: str, *, page: int = 1, limit: int = 50
6806    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
6807        """List evaluation criteria for an agent with pagination metadata.
6808
6809        Args:
6810            agent_id: Agent identifier.
6811            page: Page number (1-indexed).
6812            limit: Items per page.
6813
6814        Returns:
6815            ``{"data": [...], "pagination": {"page", "limit", "total", "pages",
6816            "has_next", "has_prev"}}`` when the client opts in with
6817            ``api_version="2026-07-27"`` or later.
6818
6819            Without that opt-in the endpoint answers with a bare, **unpaginated**
6820            array of every criterion, which is returned as ``{"data": [...]}``
6821            with no ``pagination`` key — so read it with ``.get("pagination")``
6822            rather than indexing.
6823        """
6824        result = await self.request(
6825            "GET",
6826            f"/agents/{agent_id}/evaluation-criteria",
6827            params=_strip_none({"page": page, "limit": limit}),
6828        )
6829        return _keyed_list(result, "data")

7743    async def list_source_contents(
7744        self,
7745        source_id: str,
7746        *,
7747        page: int | None = None,
7748        limit: int | None = None,
7749        sort: str | None = None,
7750        order: str | None = None,
7751        status: str | None = None,
7752        content_version_ids: list[str] | None = None,
7753    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
7754        """List a source's content items and their indexing status.
7755
7756        Args:
7757            source_id: Source identifier.
7758            page: Page number (1-indexed, default 1).
7759            limit: Items per page (1-100, default 20).
7760            sort: Sort field — ``created_at``, ``title`` or ``status``.
7761            order: ``asc`` or ``desc``.
7762            status: Keep only one status: ``pending``, ``fetching``,
7763                ``transcribing``, ``scanning``, ``indexing``, ``completed`` or
7764                ``failed``.
7765            content_version_ids: Keep only these items — the
7766                ``content_version_id`` values the upload methods return — to
7767                poll a batch of uploads in one request. Keep it to about 100:
7768                the ids travel in the query string, and a URL over 8,192 bytes
7769                is rejected with a 414. The API itself accepts at most 500.
7770
7771        Returns:
7772            ``{"data": [...], "pagination": {...}}`` on every API version. An
7773            empty ``content_version_ids`` matches nothing: an empty page is
7774            returned without sending a request.
7775        """
7776        if content_version_ids is not None and not content_version_ids:
7777            return _empty_page(page=page or 1, limit=limit or 20)
7778        return cast(
7779            dict[str, Any],
7780            await self.request(
7781                "GET",
7782                f"/sources/{source_id}/contents",
7783                params=_strip_none(
7784                    {
7785                        "page": page,
7786                        "limit": limit,
7787                        "sort": sort,
7788                        "order": order,
7789                        "status": status,
7790                        "content_version_id": content_version_ids,
7791                    }
7792                ),
7793            ),
7794        )
7795
7796    async def get_source_content_status(
7797        self, source_id: str, content_version_id: str
7798    ) -> dict[str, Any]:

7812            ),

7907    async def download_source_export(
7908        self, source_id: str, export_id: str
7909    ) -> httpx.Response:
7910        """Download a completed source export.
7911
7912        Returns a **streaming** response. The caller is responsible for
7913        consuming and closing the response::
7914
7915            response = await client.download_source_export("src", "exp")
7916            async with response:
7917                async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
7918                    f.write(chunk)
7919
7920        Args:
7921            source_id: Source identifier.
7922            export_id: Export identifier.
7923
7924        Returns:
7925            A streaming ``httpx.Response``. Must be closed by the caller.
7926        """
7927        headers = await _merge_request_headers_async(
7928            options=self._options,
7929            client_headers=self._client.headers,
7930            request_headers=None,
7931        )
7932        request = self._client.build_request(
7933            "GET",
7934            f"/sources/{source_id}/exports/{export_id}/download",
7935            headers=headers,
7936        )
7937        response = await self._client.send(request, stream=True)
7938        if response.is_error:
7939            # Read the body for a useful error message, then release the
7940            # connection before raising — the caller never receives the
7941            # streaming response on the error path.
7942            await response.aread()
7943            await response.aclose()
7944            _raise_for_status(response)
7945        return response
7946

8476    async def list_alerts(

8484        """List alerts.
8485
8486        Args:
8487            page: Page number (1-indexed).
8488            limit: Items per page.
8489            status: Filter by alert status.
8490            severity: Deprecated and ignored. The API declares no severity filter
8491                on this endpoint, so it never filtered anything, and sending it
8492                is a 422 once ``api_version`` is ``2026-07-27`` or later. It is
8493                accepted and dropped so existing call sites keep working.
8494
8495        Returns:
8496            Paginated list of alerts.
8497        """
8498        return await self.request(
8499            "GET",
8500            "/alerts",
8501            params=_strip_none({"page": page, "limit": limit, "status": status}),
8502        )

8674    async def list_model_alerts(self, *, page: int = 1, limit: int = 50) -> JSONValue:
8675        """List model alerts.
8676
8677        Args:
8678            page: Page number (1-indexed). Translated to the ``offset`` the
8679                endpoint actually declares; it does not accept ``page``, so
8680                every page but the first previously returned page 1.
8681            limit: Items per page.
8682
8683        Returns:
8684            The alerts under ``alerts`` with ``total``, on every API version. Once
8685            the client opts in with ``api_version="2026-07-27"`` or later the
8686            response also carries ``data`` and ``pagination``.
8687        """
8688        # `offset` is declared `minimum: 0`, so a defensive caller passing page=0
8689        # would turn a previously-ignored parameter into a hard 422.
8690        offset = max(page - 1, 0) * limit
8691        return _keyed_list(
8692            await self.request(
8693                "GET",
8694                "/models/alerts",
8695                params=_strip_none({"offset": offset, "limit": limit}),
8696            ),
8697            "alerts",
8698            ("total",),
8699        )
8700

9350    # ── Pagination helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
9351
9352    async def paginate(
9353        self,
9354        method: str,
9355        path: str,
9356        *,
9357        params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
9358        limit: int = 50,
9359        items_key: str = "data",
9360        param_style: Literal["page", "offset"] = "page",
9361    ) -> AsyncGenerator[dict[str, Any]]:
9362        """Auto-paginate a list endpoint, yielding items lazily.
9363
9364        Fetches pages sequentially; use ``async for item in client.paginate(...):``
9365        to iterate.
9366
9367        The walk ends after a page that is a bare array, that is short or
9368        empty, that reports ``pagination.has_next`` false, or that reaches the
9369        ``total`` the body reports. A page holding more than ``limit`` items
9370        also ends it — the endpoint ignored ``limit`` and returned everything —
9371        unless the body itself says more exist.
9372
9373        A page identical to the one before it is never yielded: the endpoint
9374        did not advance for the cursor it was sent. If that page reports more
9375        items (``has_next`` true, or a ``total`` above the number yielded) the
9376        walk raises `SeclaiError` rather than return a short result; if it
9377        reports no paging information the walk ends quietly. Two consecutive
9378        pages that are legitimately identical cannot be told apart from that,
9379        and are treated the same way.
9380
9381        Args:
9382            method: HTTP method (typically ``"GET"``).
9383            path: API path.
9384            params: Extra query parameters (the cursor and ``limit`` are managed
9385                automatically).
9386            limit: Items per page, a positive integer.
9387            items_key: Per-resource key the items sit under when the response
9388                is not the ``data`` envelope, which is always read first.
9389            param_style: ``"page"`` (default) sends a 1-indexed ``page``;
9390                ``"offset"`` sends a 0-based ``offset``. A few endpoints —
9391                ``/models/alerts`` among them — declare only ``offset``. They
9392                ignore ``page`` by default, which the walk reports as an error
9393                on the second page, and reject it with a 422 once the client
9394                opts in with ``api_version="2026-07-27"`` or later.
9395
9396        Yields:
9397            Individual items from each page.
9398
9399        Raises:
9400            ValueError: If ``param_style`` is neither ``"page"`` nor ``"offset"``,
9401                or ``limit`` is not a positive integer.
9402            SeclaiError: If a page is neither a list nor an object carrying
9403                ``data`` or ``items_key``, or if the endpoint returns the same
9404                page twice while reporting more items.
9405        """
9406        walk = _PageWalk(limit=limit, param_style=param_style)
9407        base_params = dict(params) if params else {}
9408        while not walk.finished:
9409            base_params.update(walk._next_params())
9410            result = await self.request(method, path, params=base_params)
9411            items = walk._accept(result, items_key)
9412            if items is None:
9413                break
9414            for item in items:
9415                yield item
9416
9417    # ── High-level Abstractions ───────────────────────────────────────────────
9418
9419    async def run_agent_and_poll(
9420        self,
9421        agent_id: str,
9422        body: AgentRunRequest,
9423        *,
9424        poll_interval: float = 2.0,
9425        include_step_outputs: bool = False,
9426    ) -> AgentRunResponse:
9427        """Run an agent and poll until it reaches a terminal status.
9428
9429        Starts the agent run and then repeatedly polls ``get_agent_run`` until
9430        the status is ``"completed"`` or ``"failed"``.
9431
9432        Args:
9433            agent_id: Agent identifier.
9434            body: Agent run request payload.
9435            poll_interval: Seconds between poll attempts (default 2.0).
9436            include_step_outputs: Include per-step outputs when polling.
9437
9438        Returns:
9439            The final agent run (completed or failed).
9440
9441        Raises:
9442            SeclaiAPIValidationError: If the API returns a validation error.
9443            SeclaiAPIStatusError: If the API returns a non-success status code.
9444        """
9445        import asyncio
9446
9447        run = await self.run_agent(agent_id, body)
9448        while run.status not in ("completed", "failed"):
9449            await asyncio.sleep(poll_interval)
9450            run = await self.get_agent_run(
9451                run.run_id, include_step_outputs=include_step_outputs
9452            )
9453        return run
9454
9455    async def run_streaming_agent(
9456        self,
9457        agent_id: str,
9458        body: AgentRunStreamRequest,
9459        *,
9460        timeout: float | None = None,
9461        headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
9462    ) -> AsyncGenerator[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
9463        """Run an agent via SSE streaming and yield events as they arrive.
9464
9465        Use ``async for event_type, data in client.run_streaming_agent(...)`` to
9466        process events lazily without buffering the entire stream.
9467
9468        Args:
9469            agent_id: Agent identifier.
9470            body: Streaming agent run request payload.
9471            timeout: Max time (seconds) to wait. Defaults to this client's timeout.
9472            headers: Optional extra headers.
9473
9474        Yields:
9475            ``(event_type, parsed_data)`` tuples for each SSE event.
9476
9477        Raises:
9478            SeclaiAPIStatusError: If the API returns a non-success status code.
9479            SeclaiStreamingError: If an error event is received.
9480            SeclaiError: If the stream times out.
9481        """
9482        import json as _json
9483
9484        path = f"/agents/{agent_id}/runs/stream"
9485        merged_headers = await _merge_request_headers_async(
9486            options=self._options,
9487            client_headers=self._client.headers,
9488            request_headers=headers,
9489        )
9490        _setdefault_header(merged_headers, "accept", "text/event-stream")
9491        timeout_seconds = self._options.timeout if timeout is None else timeout
9492        start = time.monotonic()
9493
9494        try:
9495            async with self._client.stream(
9496                "POST",
9497                path,
9498                json=body,
9499                headers=merged_headers,
9500                timeout=timeout_seconds,
9501            ) as response:
9502                if response.status_code >= 400:
9503                    # Lazy body inside `stream()`; read it so a 422's field-level
9504                    # detail survives into SeclaiAPIValidationError.
9505                    await response.aread()
9506                _raise_for_status(response)
9507                current_event: str | None = None
9508                data_lines: list[str] = []
9509
9510                async for line in response.aiter_lines():
9511                    if time.monotonic() - start > timeout_seconds:
9512                        raise SeclaiError(
9513                            f"Timed out after {timeout_seconds}s waiting for streaming agent run."
9514                        )
9515                    if line == "":
9516                        if current_event and data_lines:
9517                            data = "\n".join(data_lines)
9518                            try:
9519                                parsed = cast(dict[str, Any], _json.loads(data))
9520                            except Exception:
9521                                parsed = {"raw": data}
9522                            if current_event == "error":
9523                                raise SeclaiStreamingError(
9524                                    parsed.get("message", data),
9525                                    run_id=parsed.get("run_id"),
9526                                )
9527                            yield (current_event, parsed)
9528                        current_event = None
9529                        data_lines = []
9530                        continue
9531                    if line.startswith(":"):
9532                        continue
9533                    if line.startswith("event:"):
9534                        current_event = line[len("event:") :].strip() or None
9535                        continue
9536                    if line.startswith("data:"):
9537                        data_lines.append(line[len("data:") :].lstrip())
9538                        continue
9539
9540                if current_event and data_lines:
9541                    data = "\n".join(data_lines)
9542                    try:
9543                        parsed = cast(dict[str, Any], _json.loads(data))
9544                    except Exception:
9545                        parsed = {"raw": data}
9546                    if current_event == "error":
9547                        raise SeclaiStreamingError(
9548                            parsed.get("message", data),
9549                            run_id=parsed.get("run_id"),
9550                        )
9551                    yield (current_event, parsed)
9552        except httpx.TimeoutException as e:
9553            raise SeclaiError(
9554                f"Timed out after {timeout_seconds}s waiting for streaming agent run."
9555            ) from e

Seclai asynchronous client.

Most users should prefer the typed convenience methods (e.g. run_agent, list_sources) which raise SDK exceptions on failures.

This client can be used as an async context manager:

async with AsyncSeclai(api_key="...") as client:
    sources = await client.list_sources()
AsyncSeclai( *, api_key: str | None = None, access_token: str | Callable[[], str | Awaitable[str]] | None = None, timeout: float = 30.0, api_key_header: str = 'x-api-key', default_headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, http_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None, profile: str | None = None, config_dir: str | None = None, auto_refresh: bool = True, account_id: str | None = None, api_version: str | None = None, allow_unknown_api_version: bool = False) 
5242    def __init__(
5243        self,
5244        *,
5245        api_key: str | None = None,
5246        access_token: str | Callable[[], str | Awaitable[str]] | None = None,
5247        timeout: float = 30.0,
5248        api_key_header: str = "x-api-key",
5249        default_headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
5250        http_client: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None,
5251        profile: str | None = None,
5252        config_dir: str | None = None,
5253        auto_refresh: bool = True,
5254        account_id: str | None = None,
5255        api_version: str | None = None,
5256        allow_unknown_api_version: bool = False,
5257    ) -> None:
5258        """Create an asynchronous Seclai client.
5259
5260        Credentials are resolved via a chain (first match wins):
5261
5262        1. Explicit ``api_key``
5263        2. Explicit ``access_token`` (static string or provider callable)
5264        3. ``SECLAI_API_KEY`` environment variable
5265        4. SSO profile from ``~/.seclai/config`` + cached tokens
5266
5267        Args:
5268            api_key: API key used for authentication. If omitted, ``SECLAI_API_KEY`` is used.
5269            access_token: Static bearer token string or a callable returning one
5270                (sync or async). Mutually exclusive with ``api_key``.
5271            timeout: Request timeout (seconds).
5272            api_key_header: Header name to use for the API key.
5273            default_headers: Extra headers to include on every request.
5274            http_client: Optional pre-configured ``httpx.AsyncClient`` to use. A
5275                ``Seclai-Version`` among its default headers is checked as one
5276                in ``default_headers`` is, at construction and on each request.
5277                The typed methods that go through the generated client do not
5278                use this client.
5279            profile: SSO profile name from ``~/.seclai/config``.
5280            config_dir: Override the config directory path.
5281            auto_refresh: Auto-refresh expired SSO tokens. Defaults to ``True``.
5282            account_id: Target organization account ID (``X-Account-Id`` header).
5283            api_version: Dated API version (``YYYY-MM-DD``) sent as the
5284                ``Seclai-Version`` header, opting into backward-incompatible
5285                changes released on or before that date. Omitted by default,
5286                so upgrading the SDK alone never changes response shapes.
5287
5288        Raises:
5289            SeclaiConfigurationError: If no credentials are found.
5290        """
5291        super().__init__(
5292            api_key=api_key,
5293            access_token=access_token,
5294            timeout=timeout,
5295            api_key_header=api_key_header,
5296            default_headers=default_headers,
5297            profile=profile,
5298            config_dir=config_dir,
5299            auto_refresh=auto_refresh,
5300            account_id=account_id,
5301            api_version=api_version,
5302            allow_unknown_api_version=allow_unknown_api_version,
5303        )
5304        self._client = http_client or httpx.AsyncClient(
5305            base_url=SECLAI_API_URL,
5306            timeout=self._options.timeout,
5307            headers=self._default_headers(),

The typed methods that go through the generated client do not use this client. profile: SSO profile name from ~/.seclai/config. config_dir: Override the config directory path. auto_refresh: Auto-refresh expired SSO tokens. 5440        self,
5441        agent_id: str,
5442        body: AgentRunStreamRequest,
5443        *,
5444        timeout: float | None = None,
5445        headers: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
5446    ) -> AgentRunResponse:
5447        """Run an agent via SSE streaming and block until completion (async).
5448
5449        This uses POST /agents/{agent_id}/runs/stream and consumes Server-Sent Events (SSE).
5450        The method returns when an `event: done` message is received.
5451        """
5452        import json as _json
5453        import time as _time
5454
5455        path = f"/agents/{agent_id}/runs/stream"
5456
5457        merged_headers = await _merge_request_headers_async(
5458            options=self._options,
5459            client_headers=self._client.headers,
5460            request_headers=headers,
5461        )
5462        _setdefault_header(merged_headers, "accept", "text/event-stream")
5463
5464        timeout_seconds = self._options.timeout if timeout is None else timeout
5465        start = _time.monotonic()
5466
5467        try:
5468            async with self._client.stream(
5469                "POST",
5470                path,
5471                json=body,
5472                headers=merged_headers,
5473                timeout=timeout_seconds,
5474            ) as response:
5475                if response.status_code >= 400:
5476                    # Lazy body inside `stream()`; read it so the error carries
5477                    # its text and a 422 its field-level detail.
5478                    await response.aread()
5479                _raise_for_status(response)
5480
5481                current_event: str | None = None
5482                data_lines: list[str] = []
5483                last_seen: AgentRunResponse | None = None
5484
5485                def dispatch() -> AgentRunResponse | None:
5486                    nonlocal current_event, data_lines, last_seen
5487                    if current_event is None and not data_lines:
5488                        return None
5489                    data = "\n".join(data_lines)
5490                    evt = current_event
5491                    current_event = None
5492                    data_lines = []
5493                    if not data:
5494                        return None
5495                    if evt not in {"init", "done"}:
5496                        return None
5497                    try:
5498                        parsed_dict = cast(dict[str, Any], _json.loads(data))
5499                        parsed = AgentRunResponse.from_dict(parsed_dict)
5500                        last_seen = parsed
5501                        if evt == "done":
5502                            return parsed
5503                    except Exception:
5504                        return None
5505                    return None
5506
5507                async for line in response.aiter_lines():
5508                    if _time.monotonic() - start > timeout_seconds:
5509                        raise SeclaiError(
5510                            f"Timed out after {timeout_seconds}s waiting for streaming agent run to complete."
5511                        )
5512
5513                    if line == "":
5514                        done = dispatch()
5515                        if done is not None:
5516                            return done
5517                        continue
5518                    if line.startswith(":"):
5519                        continue
5520                    if line.startswith("event:"):
5521                        current_event = line[len("event:") :].strip() or None
5522                        continue
5523                    if line.startswith("data:"):
5524                        data_lines.append(line[len("data:") :].lstrip())
5525                        continue
5526
5527                done = dispatch()
5528                if done is not None:
5529                    return done
5530                if last_seen is not None:
5531                    return last_seen
5532                raise SeclaiError("Stream ended before receiving a 'done' event.")

5535                f"Timed out after {timeout_seconds}s waiting for streaming agent run to complete."

Cancel an in-progress agent run.

Cancellation is DELETE on the run resource — the API exposes no POST .../cancel route, and no operation that deletes a run. Rejected when the run has already reached a terminal state.

async def download_agent_run_attachment( self, run_id: str, attachment_id: str, *, download_name: str | None = None) -> httpx.Response: 
6622    async def download_agent_run_attachment(
6623        self,
6624        run_id: str,
6625        attachment_id: str,
6626        *,
6627        download_name: str | None = None,
6628    ) -> httpx.Response:
6629        """Download an attachment emitted by a step in an agent run.
6630
6631        Returns a **streaming** response. The caller is responsible for
6632        consuming and closing the response::
6633
6634            response = await client.download_agent_run_attachment("run", "att")
6635            async with response:
6636                async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
6637                    f.write(chunk)
6638
6639        Args:
6640            run_id: Run identifier.
6641            attachment_id: URL-safe-base64-encoded ``storage_key`` of the
6642                attachment (as surfaced in webhook/email payloads and run
6643                output manifests).
6644            download_name: Optional filename hint for the download disposition.
6645
6646        Returns:
6647            A streaming ``httpx.Response``. Must be closed by the caller.
6648        """
6649        headers = await _merge_request_headers_async(
6650            options=self._options,
6651            client_headers=self._client.headers,
6652            request_headers=None,
6653        )
6654        request = self._client.build_request(
6655            "GET",
6656            f"/v2/agent-runs/{run_id}/attachments/{attachment_id}",
6657            params=_strip_none({"download_name": download_name}),
6658            headers=headers,
6659        )
6660        response = await self._client.send(request, stream=True)
6661        if response.is_error:
6662            # Read the body for a useful error message, then release the
6663            # connection before raising — the caller never receives the
6664            # streaming response on the error path.
6665            await response.aread()
6666            await response.aclose()
6667            _raise_for_status(response)
6668        return response

Download an attachment emitted by a step in an agent run.

Returns a streaming response. The caller is responsible for consuming and closing the response::

response = await client.download_agent_run_attachment("run", "att")
async with response:
    async for chunk in response.aiter_bytes():
        f.write(chunk)

Args: run_id: Run identifier. attachment_id: URL-safe-base64-encoded storage_key of the attachment (as surfaced in webhook/email payloads and run output manifests). download_name: Optional filename hint for the download disposition.

Returns: A streaming httpx.Response. Must be closed by the caller.

7743    async def list_source_contents(
7744        self,
7745        source_id: str,
7746        *,
7747        page: int | None = None,
7748        limit: int | None = None,
7749        sort: str | None = None,
7750        order: str | None = None,
7751        status: str | None = None,
7752        content_version_ids: list[str] | None = None,
7753    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
7754        """List a source's content items and their indexing status.
7755
7756        Args:
7757            source_id: Source identifier.
7758            page: Page number (1-indexed, default 1).
7759            limit: Items per page (1-100, default 20).
7760            sort: Sort field — ``created_at``, ``title`` or ``status``.
7761            order: ``asc`` or ``desc``.
7762            status: Keep only one status: ``pending``, ``fetching``,
7763                ``transcribing``, ``scanning``, ``indexing``, ``completed`` or
7764                ``failed``.
7765            content_version_ids: Keep only these items — the
7766                ``content_version_id`` values the upload methods return — to
7767                poll a batch of uploads in one request. Keep it to about 100:
7768                the ids travel in the query string, and a URL over 8,192 bytes
7769                is rejected with a 414. The API itself accepts at most 500.
7770
7771        Returns:
7772            ``{"data": [...], "pagination": {...}}`` on every API version. An
7773            empty ``content_version_ids`` matches nothing: an empty page is
7774            returned without sending a request.
7775        """
7776        if content_version_ids is not None and not content_version_ids:
7777            return _empty_page(page=page or 1, limit=limit or 20)
7778        return cast(
7779            dict[str, Any],
7780            await self.request(
7781                "GET",
7782                f"/sources/{source_id}/contents",
7783                params=_strip_none(
7784                    {
7785                        "page": page,
7786                        "limit": limit,
7787                        "sort": sort,
7788                        "order": order,
7789                        "status": status,
7790                        "content_version_id": content_version_ids,
7791                    }
7792                ),
7793            ),
7794        )

List a source's content items and their indexing status.

Keep it to about 100: the ids travel in the query string, and a URL over 8,192 bytes is rejected with a 414. The API itself accepts at most 500.

8674    async def list_model_alerts(self, *, page: int = 1, limit: int = 50) -> JSONValue:
8675        """List model alerts.
8676
8677        Args:
8678            page: Page number (1-indexed). Translated to the ``offset`` the
8679                endpoint actually declares; it does not accept ``page``, so
8680                every page but the first previously returned page 1.
8681            limit: Items per page.
8682
8683        Returns:
8684            The alerts under ``alerts`` with ``total``, on every API version. Once
8685            the client opts in with ``api_version="2026-07-27"`` or later the
8686            response also carries ``data`` and ``pagination``.
8687        """
8688        # `offset` is declared `minimum: 0`, so a defensive caller passing page=0
8689        # would turn a previously-ignored parameter into a hard 422.
8690        offset = max(page - 1, 0) * limit
8691        return _keyed_list(
8692            await self.request(
8693                "GET",
8694                "/models/alerts",
8695                params=_strip_none({"offset": offset, "limit": limit}),
8696            ),
8697            "alerts",
8698            ("total",),
8699        )

async def paginate( self, method: str, path: str, *, params: dict[str, typing.Any] | None = None, limit: int = 50, items_key: str = 'data', param_style: Literal['page', 'offset'] = 'page') -> AsyncGenerator[dict[str, typing.Any]]: 
9352    async def paginate(
9353        self,
9354        method: str,
9355        path: str,
9356        *,
9357        params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
9358        limit: int = 50,
9359        items_key: str = "data",
9360        param_style: Literal["page", "offset"] = "page",
9361    ) -> AsyncGenerator[dict[str, Any]]:
9362        """Auto-paginate a list endpoint, yielding items lazily.
9363
9364        Fetches pages sequentially; use ``async for item in client.paginate(...):``
9365        to iterate.
9366
9367        The walk ends after a page that is a bare array, that is short or
9368        empty, that reports ``pagination.has_next`` false, or that reaches the
9369        ``total`` the body reports. A page holding more than ``limit`` items
9370        also ends it — the endpoint ignored ``limit`` and returned everything —
9371        unless the body itself says more exist.
9372
9373        A page identical to the one before it is never yielded: the endpoint
9374        did not advance for the cursor it was sent. If that page reports more
9375        items (``has_next`` true, or a ``total`` above the number yielded) the
9376        walk raises `SeclaiError` rather than return a short result; if it
9377        reports no paging information the walk ends quietly. Two consecutive
9378        pages that are legitimately identical cannot be told apart from that,
9379        and are treated the same way.
9380
9381        Args:
9382            method: HTTP method (typically ``"GET"``).
9383            path: API path.
9384            params: Extra query parameters (the cursor and ``limit`` are managed
9385                automatically).
9386            limit: Items per page, a positive integer.
9387            items_key: Per-resource key the items sit under when the response
9388                is not the ``data`` envelope, which is always read first.
9389            param_style: ``"page"`` (default) sends a 1-indexed ``page``;
9390                ``"offset"`` sends a 0-based ``offset``. A few endpoints —
9391                ``/models/alerts`` among them — declare only ``offset``. They
9392                ignore ``page`` by default, which the walk reports as an error
9393                on the second page, and reject it with a 422 once the client
9394                opts in with ``api_version="2026-07-27"`` or later.
9395
9396        Yields:
9397            Individual items from each page.
9398
9399        Raises:
9400            ValueError: If ``param_style`` is neither ``"page"`` nor ``"offset"``,
9401                or ``limit`` is not a positive integer.
9402            SeclaiError: If a page is neither a list nor an object carrying
9403                ``data`` or ``items_key``, or if the endpoint returns the same
9404                page twice while reporting more items.
9405        """
9406        walk = _PageWalk(limit=limit, param_style=param_style)
9407        base_params = dict(params) if params else {}
9408        while not walk.finished:
9409            base_params.update(walk._next_params())
9410            result = await self.request(method, path, params=base_params)
9411            items = walk._accept(result, items_key)
9412            if items is None:
9413                break
9414            for item in items:
9415                yield item

Auto-paginate a list endpoint, yielding items lazily.

Fetches pages sequentially; use async for item in client.paginate(...): to iterate.

The walk ends after a page that is a bare array, that is short or empty, that reports pagination.has_next false, or that reaches the total the body reports. A page holding more than limit items also ends it — the endpoint ignored limit and returned everything — unless the body itself says more exist.

A page identical to the one before it is never yielded: the endpoint did not advance for the cursor it was sent. If that page reports more items (has_next true, or a total above the number yielded) the walk raises SeclaiError rather than return a short result; if it reports no paging information the walk ends quietly. Two consecutive pages that are legitimately identical cannot be told apart from that, and are treated the same way.

Args: method: HTTP method (typically "GET"). path: API path. params: Extra query parameters (the cursor and limit are managed automatically). limit: Items per page, a positive integer. items_key: Per-resource key the items sit under when the response is not the data envelope, which is always read first. param_style: "page" (default) sends a 1-indexed page; "offset" sends a 0-based offset. A few endpoints — /models/alerts among them — declare only offset. They ignore page by default, which the walk reports as an error on the second page, and reject it with a 422 once the client opts in with api_version="2026-07-27" or later.

Yields: Individual items from each page.

Raises: ValueError: If param_style is neither "page" nor "offset", or limit is not a positive integer. SeclaiError: If a page is neither a list nor an object carrying data or items_key, or if the endpoint returns the same page twice while reporting more items.

 97def unwrap_items(payload: Any, *legacy_keys: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
 98    """Return the items of a version-gated list endpoint, whichever shape it used.
 99
100    Some endpoints key their list differently depending on the ``Seclai-Version``
101    the request resolves to. On the legacy baseline it is a bare JSON array or a
102    per-resource key (``configs``, ``alerts``, ``models`` and the like); from
103    ``2026-07-27`` it is the canonical
104    ``{"data": [...], "pagination": {...}}`` envelope. Both are live during the
105    rollout, so reading only one breaks the day the other arrives.
106
107    Args:
108        payload: The decoded response body.
109        legacy_keys: Per-resource keys this endpoint uses before ``2026-07-27``,
110            tried in order after ``data``.
111
112    Returns:
113        The items. Never ``None`` — an explicit ``{"data": null}`` yields ``[]``.
114
115    Raises:
116        SeclaiError: If the payload is neither a list nor an object carrying one
117            of the expected keys. Returning ``[]`` for an unrecognised envelope
118            would report "no results" for what is really a shape the client
119            cannot read, which is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty page.
120    """
121    if isinstance(payload, list):
122        return cast(list[dict[str, Any]], payload)
123    if isinstance(payload, dict):
124        for key in ("data", *legacy_keys):
125            if key in payload:
126                items = payload[key]
127                if items is None:
128                    return []
129                if isinstance(items, list):
130                    return cast(list[dict[str, Any]], items)
131                raise SeclaiError(
132                    f"Expected a list under {key!r}, got {type(items).__name__}."
133                )
134        expected = ", ".join(repr(k) for k in ("data", *legacy_keys))
135        raise SeclaiError(
136            f"Unrecognised list response: expected a bare array or an object "
137            f"with one of {expected}, got keys {sorted(payload)}."
138        )
139    raise SeclaiError(
140        f"Unrecognised list response: expected a list or object, "
141        f"got {type(payload).__name__}."
142    )

1967            ``effective_version`` for THIS request, plus ``default_version``,
1968            ``latest_version`` and ``known_versions``. Resolution order is the
1969            ``Seclai-Version`` header, then the account pin, then the default, so
1970            ``effective_version`` reflects the client's ``api_version`` when set.
1971        """
1972        return cast(dict[str, Any], self.request("GET", "/version"))
1973
1974    def update_api_version(self, version: str | None) -> dict[str, Any]:
1975        """Pin the account to a dated API version, or clear the pin.
1976
1977        Owner/admin only.
1978
1979        Args:
1980            version: A ``YYYY-MM-DD`` date to pin to, or ``None`` to clear the pin
1981                and revert to the default baseline.
1982
1983        Returns:
1984            The updated version state. ``effective_version`` describes this
1985            request, not the pin just written — a ``Seclai-Version`` header still
1986            overrides the pin.
1987
1988        Raises:
1989            SeclaiConfigurationError: If ``version`` is one this release was not
1990                built against. The pin is account-wide and sticky, so an unknown
1991                version here would silently reshape responses for every
1992                header-less caller on the account, not just this client — a wider
1993                blast radius than the ``api_version`` option the constructor
1994                already guards. Pass ``allow_unknown_api_version=True`` to the
1995                client to override.
1996        """
1997        try:
1998            validate_api_version(
1999                version, allow_unknown=self._options.allow_unknown_api_version
2000            )
2001        except ValueError as e:
2002            raise SeclaiConfigurationError(str(e)) from e
2003        return cast(
2004            dict[str, Any],
2005            self.request("PUT", "/version", json={"version": version}),
2006        )

2235    def upload_agent_input(
2236        self,
2237        agent_id: str,
2238        *,
2239        file: bytes | str | os.PathLike[str] | BinaryIO,
2240        file_name: str | None = None,
2241        mime_type: str | None = None,
2242    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
2243        """Upload a file as input for an agent run.
2244
2245        Args:
2246            agent_id: Agent identifier.
2247            file: File payload (bytes, path, or file-like).
2248            file_name: Filename to send.
2249            mime_type: MIME type of the file.
2250
2251        Returns:
2252            Upload response with the input upload ID.
2253        """
2254        payload, created = self._prepare_upload_payload(file, file_name, mime_type)
2255        try:
2256            response = self._client.post(
2257                f"/agents/{agent_id}/upload-input",
2258                files={"file": payload},
2259                headers=_merge_request_headers(
2260                    options=self._options,
2261                    client_headers=self._client.headers,
2262                    request_headers=None,
2263                ),
2264            )
2265            _raise_for_status(response)
2266            return cast(dict[str, Any], response.json())
2267        finally:
2268            if created is not None:
2269                created.close()

2314    def download_agent_run_attachment(
2315        self,
2316        run_id: str,
2317        attachment_id: str,
2318        *,
2319        download_name: str | None = None,
2320    ) -> httpx.Response:
2321        """Download an attachment emitted by a step in an agent run.
2322
2323        Returns a **streaming** response. The caller is responsible for
2324        consuming and closing the response::
2325
2326            response = client.download_agent_run_attachment("run", "att")
2327            with response:
2328                for chunk in response.iter_bytes():
2329                    f.write(chunk)
2330
2331        Args:
2332            run_id: Run identifier.
2333            attachment_id: URL-safe-base64-encoded ``storage_key`` of the
2334                attachment (as surfaced in webhook/email payloads and run
2335                output manifests).
2336            download_name: Optional filename hint for the download disposition.
2337
2338        Returns:
2339            A streaming ``httpx.Response``. Must be closed by the caller.
2340        """
2341        request = self._client.build_request(
2342            "GET",
2343            f"/v2/agent-runs/{run_id}/attachments/{attachment_id}",
2344            params=_strip_none({"download_name": download_name}),
2345            headers=_merge_request_headers(
2346                options=self._options,
2347                client_headers=self._client.headers,
2348                request_headers=None,
2349            ),
2350        )
2351        response = self._client.send(request, stream=True)
2352        if response.is_error:
2353            # Read the body for a useful error message, then release the
2354            # connection before raising — the caller never receives the
2355            # streaming response on the error path.
2356            response.read()
2357            response.close()
2358            _raise_for_status(response)
2359        return response

3420    def list_source_contents(
3421        self,
3422        source_id: str,
3423        *,
3424        page: int | None = None,
3425        limit: int | None = None,
3426        sort: str | None = None,
3427        order: str | None = None,
3428        status: str | None = None,
3429        content_version_ids: list[str] | None = None,
3430    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
3431        """List a source's content items and their indexing status.
3432
3433        Args:
3434            source_id: Source identifier.
3435            page: Page number (1-indexed, default 1).
3436            limit: Items per page (1-100, default 20).
3437            sort: Sort field — ``created_at``, ``title`` or ``status``.
3438            order: ``asc`` or ``desc``.
3439            status: Keep only one status: ``pending``, ``fetching``,
3440                ``transcribing``, ``scanning``, ``indexing``, ``completed`` or
3441                ``failed``.
3442            content_version_ids: Keep only these items — the
3443                ``content_version_id`` values the upload methods return — to
3444                poll a batch of uploads in one request. Keep it to about 100:
3445                the ids travel in the query string, and a URL over 8,192 bytes
3446                is rejected with a 414. The API itself accepts at most 500.
3447
3448        Returns:
3449            ``{"data": [...], "pagination": {...}}`` on every API version. An
3450            empty ``content_version_ids`` matches nothing: an empty page is
3451            returned without sending a request.
3452        """
3453        if content_version_ids is not None and not content_version_ids:
3454            return _empty_page(page=page or 1, limit=limit or 20)
3455        return cast(
3456            dict[str, Any],
3457            self.request(
3458                "GET",
3459                f"/sources/{source_id}/contents",
3460                params=_strip_none(
3461                    {
3462                        "page": page,
3463                        "limit": limit,
3464                        "sort": sort,
3465                        "order": order,
3466                        "status": status,
3467                        "content_version_id": content_version_ids,
3468                    }
3469                ),
3470            ),
3471        )
3472

3484        """
3485        return cast(

3488        )

3580    def download_source_export(self, source_id: str, export_id: str) -> httpx.Response:
3581        """Download a completed source export.
3582
3583        Returns a **streaming** response. The caller is responsible for
3584        consuming and closing the response::
3585
3586            response = client.download_source_export("src", "exp")
3587            with response:
3588                for chunk in response.iter_bytes():
3589                    f.write(chunk)
3590
3591        Args:
3592            source_id: Source identifier.
3593            export_id: Export identifier.
3594
3595        Returns:
3596            A streaming ``httpx.Response``. Must be closed by the caller.
3597        """
3598        request = self._client.build_request(
3599            "GET",
3600            f"/sources/{source_id}/exports/{export_id}/download",
3601            headers=_merge_request_headers(
3602                options=self._options,
3603                client_headers=self._client.headers,
3604                request_headers=None,
3605            ),
3606        )
3607        response = self._client.send(request, stream=True)
3608        if response.is_error:
3609            # Read the body for a useful error message, then release the
3610            # connection before raising — the caller never receives the
3611            # streaming response on the error path.
3612            response.read()
3613            response.close()
3614            _raise_for_status(response)
3615        return response
3616

4143        status: str | None = None,

4145    ) -> JSONValue:
4146        """List alerts.
4147
4148        Args:
4149            page: Page number (1-indexed).
4150            limit: Items per page.
4151            status: Filter by alert status.
4152            severity: Deprecated and ignored. The API declares no severity filter
4153                on this endpoint, so it never filtered anything, and sending it
4154                is a 422 once ``api_version`` is ``2026-07-27`` or later. It is
4155                accepted and dropped so existing call sites keep working.
4156
4157        Returns:
4158            Paginated list of alerts.
4159        """

4332    def list_model_alerts(self, *, page: int = 1, limit: int = 50) -> JSONValue:
4333        """List model alerts.
4334
4335        Args:
4336            page: Page number (1-indexed). Translated to the ``offset`` the
4337                endpoint actually declares; it does not accept ``page``, so
4338                every page but the first previously returned page 1.
4339            limit: Items per page.
4340
4341        Returns:
4342            The alerts under ``alerts`` with ``total``, on every API version. Once
4343            the client opts in with ``api_version="2026-07-27"`` or later the
4344            response also carries ``data`` and ``pagination``.
4345        """
4346        # `offset` is declared `minimum: 0`, so a defensive caller passing page=0
4347        # would turn a previously-ignored parameter into a hard 422.
4348        offset = max(page - 1, 0) * limit
4349        return _keyed_list(
4350            self.request(
4351                "GET",
4352                "/models/alerts",
4353                params=_strip_none({"offset": offset, "limit": limit}),
4354            ),
4355            "alerts",
4356            ("total",),
4357        )
4358

4997    # ── Pagination helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4998
4999    def paginate(
5000        self,
5001        method: str,
5002        path: str,
5003        *,
5004        params: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
5005        limit: int = 50,
5006        items_key: str = "data",
5007        param_style: Literal["page", "offset"] = "page",
5008    ) -> Generator[dict[str, Any]]:
5009        """Auto-paginate a list endpoint.
5010
5011        Yields individual items from each page.
5012
5013        The walk ends after a page that is a bare array, that is short or
5014        empty, that reports ``pagination.has_next`` false, or that reaches the
5015        ``total`` the body reports. A page holding more than ``limit`` items
5016        also ends it — the endpoint ignored ``limit`` and returned everything —
5017        unless the body itself says more exist.
5018
5019        A page identical to the one before it is never yielded: the endpoint
5020        did not advance for the cursor it was sent. If that page reports more
5021        items (``has_next`` true, or a ``total`` above the number yielded) the
5022        walk raises `SeclaiError` rather than return a short result; if it
5023        reports no paging information the walk ends quietly. Two consecutive
5024        pages that are legitimately identical cannot be told apart from that,
5025        and are treated the same way.
5026
5027        Args:
5028            method: HTTP method (typically ``"GET"``).
5029            path: API path.
5030            params: Extra query parameters (the cursor and ``limit`` are managed
5031                automatically).
5032            limit: Items per page, a positive integer.
5033            items_key: Per-resource key the items sit under when the response
5034                is not the ``data`` envelope, which is always read first.
5035            param_style: ``"page"`` (default) sends a 1-indexed ``page``;
5036                ``"offset"`` sends a 0-based ``offset``. A few endpoints —
5037                ``/models/alerts`` among them — declare only ``offset``. They
5038                ignore ``page`` by default, which the walk reports as an error
5039                on the second page, and reject it with a 422 once the client
5040                opts in with ``api_version="2026-07-27"`` or later.
5041
5042        Yields:
5043            Individual item dicts from each page.
5044
5045        Raises:
5046            ValueError: If ``param_style`` is neither ``"page"`` nor ``"offset"``,
5047                or ``limit`` is not a positive integer.
5048            SeclaiError: If a page is neither a list nor an object carrying
5049                ``data`` or ``items_key``, or if the endpoint returns the same
5050                page twice while reporting more items.
5051        """
5052        walk = _PageWalk(limit=limit, param_style=param_style)
5053        base_params = dict(params) if params else {}
5054        while not walk.finished:
5055            base_params.update(walk._next_params())
5056            result = self.request(method, path, params=base_params)
5057            items = walk._accept(result, items_key)
5058            if items is None:
5059                return
5060            yield from items
5061

5064    def run_agent_and_poll(
5065        self,
5066        agent_id: str,
5067        body: AgentRunRequest,
5068        *,
5069        poll_interval: float = 2.0,
5070        include_step_outputs: bool = False,
5071    ) -> AgentRunResponse:
5072        """Run an agent and poll until it reaches a terminal status.
5073
5074        Starts the agent run and then repeatedly polls ``get_agent_run`` until
5075        the status is ``"completed"`` or ``"failed"``.
5076
5077        Args:
5078            agent_id: Agent identifier.
5079            body: Agent run request payload.
5080            poll_interval: Seconds between poll attempts (default 2.0).
5081            include_step_outputs: Include per-step outputs when polling.
5082
5083        Returns:
5084            The final agent run (completed or failed).
5085
5086        Raises:
5087            SeclaiAPIValidationError: If the API returns a validation error.
5088            SeclaiAPIStatusError: If the API returns a non-success status code.
5089        """
5090        run = self.run_agent(agent_id, body)
5091        while run.status not in ("completed", "failed"):
5092            time.sleep(poll_interval)
5093            run = self.get_agent_run(
5094                run.run_id, include_step_outputs=include_step_outputs
5095            )
5096        return run
